Hello, I am TrulyMadScientist. I was abruptly diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder II in August 2013 after a bout of mania that included delusional thinking. For roughly five months following I experienced major depression that I had previously never known. I did not have much of an appetite. I slept 11 hours daily and woke feeling more exhausted than I did before falling asleep. I dreaded waking. I hoped for death. It was rough.

I began feeling more like myself (only wanted to die like 1/3 of the time) in March 2014. I do not know what triggered me back into a normalized existence (sunshine of springtime?), but I was getting better. Everything was back to my "normal". Time passed by like it always does and I got tired of the side effects of my medication. It started as honest, forgetful mistakes of simply forgetting to take the meds. Then I realized that my nausea and headaches began to fade, so, without consulting with my psychiatrist first, I went off of my meds sometime in the beginning of 2016.

Work became stressful (like it does sometimes) and I began experiencing a higher-than-usual level of anxiety sometime in March 2016. My mind raced and raced, and I paced and paced. Finally (over the course of a week or so?), I consulted a professional -- a General Practitioner for anxiety; my 3-month appointment with my psychiatrist was still a few weeks away. I informed him that I had gone off of my medication for my manic depression because of the aforementioned side effects. The GP recommended, of course, to consult with my psych ASAP and he had a nurse perform an EKG to check on my heart (my BPM was quite higher than my usual). My heart was fine and healthy, and I went promptly to the pharmacy to pick up my script for Xanax after getting checked out.

Later that day (or week?) I booked an appointment with my therapist to work through my anxiety and to plan my next step. The appointment went well, but, in spite of that, things began to spiral and the delusional thoughts began creeping in again.

The delusions kept me in the hospital for much longer the second time around. First time was three nights (after which, I was still delusional walking out of the door). This time, in April 2016, I stayed for two weeks.

When I left the hospital at the end of April, I was a little delusional, a little manic, and a whole lot of anxious. Going from having my day planned out for me to having so many choices of doing whatever the hell that I wanted was overwhelming. Anxiety really sucks.

For the time being, I meet with my therapist weekly and my psychiatrist monthly. Anxiety is getting better, I just have to be patient and take it one day at a time. Overall, I am happy. For the first time in years, I am excited about living the shit out of my life.
